text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Twenty-one MPs accuse President Lennart Meri of overstepping his powers and ignoring the constitution, referring to a statement by Meri on Estonia-Russia relations.
- A Russian diplomat announced that Moscow may consider returning archive materials to the Baltic states provided they will not be used for witch hunt.
- Prime Minister Tiit Vahi expressed satisfaction with economic growth rate and declared confidence in the government coalition.
- Estonia will receive two old minesweepers from Germany, the navy commander announced.
- The port pilot service is planning to become independent of the Maritime Board, taking advantage of the government cost-cutting drive.
- The ruling coalition may break up due to conflict araund budget as the Country People's Association opposes increased defence spending and excises and demands customs barriers.
- Parliamentarians consider the planned 2.9 million kroon installation of a new electronic voting system too expensive and claim that the existing system is perfectly adequate.
- The Port of Tallin will be reorganised from state-owned enterprise into a joint-stock company.
- Japanese JEXIM Bank has offered a 330 million loan to Estonia for the development of small business, but Finance Ministry experts warn against overheating of banks.
